findings.reason: a later coordinator asking that plan whether the mismatch is already owned is sent to an unrelated landing measure, so the discharged work reads as owned when no section carries it.
findings.text: §1 says "that mismatch is `work-is-never-stuck-behind-the-admission-loop` §29's", but that plan's §29 is "The lander measures the population before it lands" (a landing gate over an importer population); the obligation row that reads "waiting for a lane slot" is discussed in §13 of the same plan ("a request admission has stalled reads the same as one that is simply queued") and `held-by-gate` appears in its §15, not §29

findings.reason: the done-when's third arm (calling `_validated_batch_waits` without `read_own_verdict`) and its negative control pin both edits, so a builder that reads the sentence as a description of existing behaviour fails the named gate rather than landing a wrong fix.
findings.text: §2 states that `_validated_batch_waits` "reads a node's own verdict only when its caller's `read_own_verdict` and `_needs_own_section_verdict(node)` both hold", but at HEAD the sole guard is `read_own_verdict` (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:2328`) and `_needs_own_section_verdict` (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:2927-2934`) carries no role test, so both stated conditions are targets rather than facts; the same sentence names `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:333` as the batch path while that file is outside the declared write paths, leaving the builder to infer that the whole change lands inside `_validated_batch_waits`

response_events.note: §1 now names admission-loop §13 and §15, which own the lane-slot wording and held-by-gate

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §1 assigns the obligation-row mismatch to `work-is-never-stuck-behind-the-admission-loop` §29, and that section is about the lander's population measurement.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §2's three arms discriminate against HEAD (today `_needs_own_section_verdict` returns True for a review node, so both paths do emit the readiness ref) and a concrete negative control is named.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the gate is a named test file inside the repository plus ruff on the staged paths; no scratchpad or node-local path is named.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the plan binds to the existing `REVIEW_ROLE` constant and adds no `"review"` literal and no plan label or ticket number to code.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §2 states as present fact two conditions the code does not carry, and the sentence that names `dispatch.py` as the batch path can read as an edit site outside the declared write paths.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §2 carries one deliverable: the role test that releases a review from its section's readiness verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `plan-after` names `work-is-never-stuck-behind-the-admission-loop`, which exists, and the section declares no dependency it does not consume.
